title: Theo and the Protocol
premise: Yara Almeida has spent eleven years alone tending Earth's last seed vault, broadcasting maintenance logs to a colony on Kepler-44 that stopped answering years ago. When the ship Meridian returns from deep space with a crew mysteriously aged backward, Yara discovers their rejuvenation was bought with a massacre aboard the colony — a massacre erased from every synchronized record. As the Meridian's crew, led by the charming Commander Ilsa Rehn, consolidates power over Earth's remaining institutions, Yara races to reconstruct the truth from her own uncorrupted vault archives and the fragmented memories of a regressed crew member named Theo. In the end, Yara broadcasts the proof to every surviving outpost at terrible personal cost, toppling Rehn's regime but leaving humanity to reckon with a history it chose to forget.
about_author: Kestrel Vane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obsolete data formats before turning to fiction. They write near-future science fiction about memory, institutions, and the people who keep records when no one else will.

chapters.title: The Last Gardener
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Establishes her solitary life in the seed vault: checking germination trays, logging temperatures, sending daily reports into silence. The emotional beat is quiet devotion tinged with grief for a colony that no longer answers.

chapters.title: Signal Decay
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She reviews eleven years of unanswered transmissions and admits to herself the colony may be gone, but keeps broadcasting anyway. A routine deep-space ping detects an inbound vessel. Hope and dread arrive together.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The ship Meridian lands near the vault. Its crew steps out impossibly young — faces she recognizes from mission footage, decades younger than they should be. The beat is uncanny wonder curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Regressed
chapters.summary: Theo's POV (first appearance). Aboard the Meridian, Theo struggles with gaps in his memory and a body too young for his service record. Crewmates deflect his questions with rehearsed smiles. He feels like a stranger in his own skin.

chapters.title: Quarantine Protocols
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Commander Ilsa Rehn visits the vault, charming and precise, requesting access to its independent archive 'for reconciliation.' Yara notices the Meridian's records don't match her own logs of the departure date. First lie detected.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Flashback chapter: how Yara came to the vault after her brother joined the Kepler-44 colony, and why she stayed when funding collapsed. Deepens her loyalty to the forgotten and sets up her personal stake.

chapters.title: What the Vault Remembers
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She compares the Meridian's official manifest against her air-gapped backups and finds the colony's final year missing — replaced by a smooth, plausible gap. Someone edited history, but not hers. Not yet.

chapters.title: A Face from the Manifest
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Among the young crew she recognizes Dr. Amara Osei, listed as dead in the colony's last transmission — yet here she is, alive and twenty-five. Yara realizes the rejuvenation and the deaths are connected.

chapters.title: Reconciliation
chapters.summary: Rehn's POV. Rehn meets with Earth's caretaker government, offering the Meridian's longevity technology in exchange for authority over communications networks. The beat is seduction — power offered generously, terms buried in warmth.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Was Old
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo wanders the vault grounds and meets Yara. Fragments surface: alarms, a corridor, someone screaming his name. He doesn't know why he trusts her, only that being near her vault feels like remembering.

chapters.title: Checksum
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara verifies her archives against physical seed-bank paper records predating network sync. The evidence holds: the colony transmitted a distress call 400 days before the Meridian returned. She begins building a case.

chapters.title: Terms of Generosity
chapters.summary: Rehn's POV. Rehn distributes longevity treatments to Earth's elite, binding them to her. Dissenting officials receive treatment delays. The corruption theme surfaces: power corrupts not through cruelty first, but through favors.

chapters.title: Night Visitor
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo secretly returns to the vault, drawn by dreams he can't explain. Yara shows him the distress transmission. Hearing it, he vomits — his body remembers what his mind lost. Alliance formed in shock.

chapters.title: The Edited Year
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Reconstruction montage: piecing together the colony's final months from partial packets, supply manifests, and orbital debris tracking. The picture emerges — the Meridian arrived early, took what it needed, and left no witnesses.

chapters.title: Longevity
chapters.summary: Rehn's POV. Rehn confronts the cost of the protocol: each rejuvenation cycle requires viable human neural tissue from unregenerated subjects. She tells herself the colony was already dying. The beat is self-justification hardening into doctrine.

chapters.title: Audit
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Government auditors arrive at the vault with warrants — Rehn's first move against her. They seize her networked systems but miss the air-gapped core. Yara plays the obedient caretaker while copying everything to seed-tray microfilm.

chapters.title: Amara Osei, Twice
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Amara, regressed like Theo, begins experiencing intrusive memories of the colony — a greenhouse, a child's drawing, fire suppression foam. Unlike Theo, she reports her flashes to Rehn. Loyalty vs. truth splits the regressed crew.

chapters.title: The Microfilm Garden
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara hides her evidence among the vault's living collection, labeling trays with ciphered accession numbers. The beat is defiant tenderness: burying truth in the one place built to outlast catastrophe.

chapters.title: Rehn's Version
chapters.summary: Rehn's POV. Public broadcast: the Meridian announces the colony died of an engineered blight; the crew risked everything to bring back the cure. Crowds weep with gratitude. Yara watches, understanding that a beautiful lie travels faster than any proof.

chapters.title: Theo Remembers Fire
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Under stress, Theo's memories flood back: he sealed a habitat door on Rehn's order while people pounded on the other side. He confesses to Yara. The beat is horror and the beginning of accountability.

chapters.title: The Witness Problem
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara realizes testimony from regressed minds will be dismissed as confabulation. She needs corroboration: the colony's black box, which orbital tracking suggests still sits in Kepler-44's debris field. Impossible distance, shrinking time.

chapters.title: Osei's Doubt
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Amara cross-references her own flash-memories against the official record and finds contradictions she can't unsee. She approaches Yara in secret, terrified. The regressed crew begins to fracture.

chapters.title: Housecleaning
chapters.summary: Rehn's POV. Rehn orders Amara 're-treated' — a deeper wipe. Theo learns of it and understands he is next. The beat is cold administrative evil: atrocities processed as scheduling.

chapters.title: Theft of a Ship
chapters.summary: Theo and Yara's alternating POV. With Amara's stolen access codes, Theo commandeers the Meridian's shuttle. Yara abandons the vault she guarded for eleven years. The beat is grief transmuted into velocity.

chapters.title: Debris Field
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The long transit to Kepler-44. Theo's memories return in full as they approach the place they happened. He describes the massacre to Yara in detail she records but cannot bear. Confession as navigation.

chapters.title: Kepler-44
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. They reach the colony: a frozen tomb, habitats breached from inside by force, not blight. Yara walks corridors her brother once walked. She finds his quarters, his plants still alive under emergency lights. Devastation and love.

chapters.title: Black Box
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. They recover the colony's black box from the comms tower. Its logs are intact — unsynced, unedited. Yara's brother's final transmission names the Meridian. Proof secured; now they must survive the trip home.

chapters.title: Intercept
chapters.summary: Rehn's POV. Rehn's loyalist ship intercepts them at the edge of the system. Amara, half-wiped but defiant, sabotages the interceptor's targeting from within. The escape costs the shuttle its long-range comms. Silence again — but this time chosen.

chapters.title: Broadcast Rights
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Home again, they find Earth locked down under Rehn's communication authority. Every channel is hers. Yara realizes the only network Rehn doesn't control is the vault's ancient, derided low-bandwidth agricultural array.

chapters.title: The Siege of the Vault
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Rehn's forces surround the vault demanding surrender. Yara stalls negotiations while Theo and Amara wire the broadcast array. The beat is a fortress of seeds and paper versus soldiers — patience weaponized.

chapters.title: What Grows Back
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. During the siege lull, Yara tends the trays one last time, knowing she may die here. Reflection on stewardship: she kept things alive for people who never came. Now the keeping becomes resistance.

chapters.title: Rehn Descends
chapters.summary: Rehn's POV. Rehn enters the vault personally, certain charm will finish what force started. She offers Yara treatment, youth, a place in the new world. Yara asks her one question: 'What was my brother's name?' Rehn doesn't know. The mask slips.

chapters.title: Uplink
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. As soldiers breach the archive levels, Theo triggers the broadcast — the black box logs, the distress call, the massacre evidence streaming across the old array to every outpost, ship, and settlement listening on legacy bands.

chapters.title: The Listening Dark
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV vignettes. Across the system, miners, station crews, and colony holdouts receive the transmission. Some refuse to believe; some recognize loved ones' voices in the final logs. Truth spreads like spores on wind.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Rehn's POV. Rehn's coalition collapses as treated elites calculate that association is now liability. Soldiers at the vault stand down mid-operation. Rehn orders a final assault no one executes. Power revealed as consensus, dissolving in real time.

chapters.title: Accounting
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Rehn is taken into custody by her own former officers. Yara insists on testifying alongside Theo — the perpetrator and the archivist side by side. The beat is justice without satisfaction: nothing brings back the colony.

chapters.title: Sentences
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The tribunal. Theo pleads guilty to his role in sealing the door, accepting judgment even though he was regressed and coerced. Amara testifies through her damaged memory. Accountability as the only honest inheritance.

chapters.title: Reseeding
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Months later: the vault reopens as a public institution, its archives made the standard for all off-world records. Yara trains a new generation of caretakers. Her brother's seed varieties are planted on Kepler-44's repaired soil.

chapters.title: Protocol
chapters.summary: Yara and Theo's shared closing POV. On the anniversary, Yara broadcasts the colony's full history — the massacre and the lives, not just the death — so remembrance outlives outrage. Final line echoes her first log entry: 'Day one. Everything recorded. Nothing forgotten.'
